newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Dostum's north Afghan town said fallen to foes.
newsitem.headline: Dostum's north Afghan town said fallen to foes.

text.p: The northern Afghan town of Shibarghan, a stronghold of opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, fell to his opponents on Saturday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted sources in Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia as saying the town, capital of Jozjan province, was captured by anti-Dostum forces led by Taleban leader Abdul Razzaq, governor of Herat. There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.
The report of Shibarghan's fall came hours after three jet fighters of Dostum's air force defected to his opponents, and only a day after Western reporters visited the town to find it calm.
The three aircraft were flown by deserters, defecting Major General Yussef Shah told reporters in the Afghan capital Kabul.
Two planes -- Soviet-built Su-22 fighter bombers -- flew from Shibarghan to Maimana, capital of Faryab province, and one -- an L39 Albatross jet trainer -- was taken to Kabul.
